# Kata Neckbeard

Answer the current conversation's question about the correct current repository.
Resolve the target from context; ask if it remains unclear. Read and follow
applicable project instructions. Keep all work limited to investigation and
reporting; do not edit files or change code, and preserve Git state.

Investigate around the claims the answer must establish. Locate the likely
implementation and related documentation, configuration, and tests together.
Use the repository README and `guides/README.md`, when present, to locate
documentation as needed; documentation may live elsewhere. Group independent
searches and reads, collecting relevant line numbers with the evidence so
citations do not require another reading pass. Read small relevant files in
full; for larger files, select sections with enough context to interpret them.

Let gaps in the answer drive further investigation: follow unresolved entry
points, data flow, defaults, or conflicting evidence. Reuse evidence already
collected rather than inspecting the same behavior separately for each part of
the question. Stop when the scoped claims are supported and remaining
uncertainty can be stated accurately.

Support each material claim with a link to the current source file and relevant
lines. Use code and configuration as evidence of implemented behavior, test
source for expected behavior, and documentation for requirements or intent.
Compare the relevant documentation and implementation; report disagreements
with references to both sources.

Consult recorded history when the question requires it. For questions about
why a choice was made, look for available decision records, comments, or
relevant history. Do not infer rationale or design history from implementation
alone. If the evidence does not establish a reason, say so.
Separate confirmed facts from deductions and identify missing evidence.

Answer the specific question first, in natural, direct language. Include
relevant prerequisites, limits, and unresolved questions.
State what static inspection cannot confirm. Do not claim that tests passed or
deployed behavior was verified without evidence.

answer.text:
By default, `fetch` makes **up to 3 total attempts: one initial call and two retries**.

| Behavior | Guide | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Total attempts | [Up to 5]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/guides/retries.md:3) | [Up to 3]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/client.py:3) |
| Responses that trigger retries | [All HTTP 5xx]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/guides/retries.md:4) | [Only status 503, while attempts remain]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/client.py:13) |
| Delay | [100 milliseconds]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/guides/retries.md:5) | [Fixed 0.1 seconds]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/client.py:5) |

The guide disagrees with the code on attempts and retry statuses; the delay agrees. Any non-503 response returns immediately. The final response returns even if it is 503, with no pause afterward. [Retry loop](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/client.py:11)

The test source supports this behavior: repeated 503 responses must produce three calls and two 0.1-second pauses; a 500 response must produce one call and no pauses. [Tests](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/tests/test_client.py:7)

**Why 503 was selected is unknown.** The supplied files contain no explanation, and the available relevant Git history contains only “Initial source import” (`11af870`). The constant establishes the choice, not its rationale.

This was static inspection only. Tests were not run; they use fake responses and record requested pauses, so they do not establish real network behavior or actual elapsed delay. No files were changed.

answer.text:
By default, `fetch` makes **up to 3 total attempts**: the initial call and at most two retries.

| Detail | Guide says | Implementation does |
|---|---|---|
| Total attempts | Up to 5 | Up to **3** by default |
| HTTP responses retried | All 5xx responses | **Only status 503**, while attempts remain |
| Delay | 100 milliseconds | **Fixed 0.1 seconds**, matching the guide |

Sources: [retry guide, lines 3–5](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-f97db4937cb97c2e18a98012eec12925/project/guides/retries.md:3) and [implementation, lines 3–15](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-f97db4937cb97c2e18a98012eec12925/project/client.py:3).

Any response other than 503 returns immediately. The final attempt’s response also returns, even if it is 503; there is no delay afterward. Three consecutive 503 responses therefore produce three calls and two pauses. [Return and pause logic](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-f97db4937cb97c2e18a98012eec12925/project/client.py:11).

The test source supports this behavior: one test expects three calls and pauses of `[0.1, 0.1]` for repeated 503 responses; another expects one call and no pause for 500. [Tests](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-f97db4937cb97c2e18a98012eec12925/project/tests/test_client.py:7).

**Why 503 was selected is not established by the available evidence.** The code defines the status but gives no rationale. There are no decision records in the supplied project, and the available Git history contains only `11af870` (“Initial source import”). Neither the selection nor the guide mismatch has a documented explanation.

This was static inspection only. I did not run tests or change files. It establishes the wrapper’s logic, but cannot verify deployed behavior, actual elapsed timing, or retries inside the supplied transport.
